title: Tensor base-change hypotheses after localization at contracted primes
statement: Let Λ be a preorder, A,B:Λ→CommRing functors, η:A→B, and κ:B→const S a cocone to a commutative ring S. Let D:Λ→AddCommGrp, with D_i a B_i-module and D transitions semilinear over B transitions. For each i→j assume a ring isomorphism B_i⊗_{A_i}A_j≃B_j with value b⊗a↦B(i→j)(b)η_j(a), and a B_j-linear isomorphism B_j⊗_{B_i}D_i≃D_j with value b⊗x↦b D(i→j)(x). For q∈Spec S, set q_i=κ_i⁻¹q, p_i=η_i⁻¹q_i, Aq_i=(A_i)_{p_i}, Bq_i=(B_i)_{q_i}, and Nq_i=(D_i)_{q_i}, with canonical fraction maps. For every i→j there are a ring map t:Bq_i⊗_{Aq_i}Aq_j→Bq_j and a submonoid W of its source such that Bq_j is the localization at W and t(b⊗a)=Bq(i→j)(b)φ_j(a), where φ_j:Aq_j→Bq_j is the canonical local map. There is also a Bq_j-linear isomorphism Bq_j⊗_{Bq_i}Nq_i≃Nq_j sending b⊗x to b Nq(i→j)(x). There is no directedness, colimit, finiteness, or flatness assumption. Tensor and localization mean [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and q is a point of [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

proof.text: Naturality identifies the contracted primes and gives the commuting square of canonical local ring maps (primeDiagramHom_naturality). Bundle the two maps to the localized target as algebra homomorphisms and construct t using Algebra.TensorProduct.productMap; its pure-tensor formula is definitional.

For a single transition, construct the numerator map θ from B_i tensor over A_i with A_j to B_i,q_i tensor over A_i,p_i with A_j,p_j. The proved private lemma localizedTensor_isLocalization first applies IsLocalization.tensorProduct_tensorProduct to localize the left factor, then tensorProduct_tensorProduct_right to localize the right factor. Compose the two localizations and transport along IsLocalization.algebraTensorEquiv, which changes the tensor base from A_i to A_i,p_i without changing pure tensors. Thus θ is a localization at a submonoid M of the original tensor ring.

The original tensor isomorphism e and its given formula imply t composed with θ equals the localization map B_j to B_j,q_j composed with e; verify equality on the two tensor inclusions. Transport the localization of B_j at q_j across e to obtain a localization of the original tensor at N=q_j-complement mapped by e inverse. Each element of M maps to a unit under θ and hence under t, so its image under e lies outside q_j. Thus M is contained in N. IsLocalization.isLocalization_of_submonoid_le now makes t a localization at θ(N); use this submonoid as W.

The original module tensor isomorphism gives IsBaseChange for the transition map. The two module localization maps are base changes by IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange. Compose the original base change with localization of the target using IsBaseChange.comp. The explicitly defined primeModuleMap, restricted to original numerators, agrees with this composite (primeModuleMap_mk at denominator one). Cancel localization of the source with IsBaseChange.of_comp. Its canonical equivalence IsBaseChange.equiv is the required localized tensor equivalence, and equiv_tmul gives precisely the stated formula. The private helper primeModuleMap_baseChange proves this for arbitrary compatible prime ideals, without ring-tensor, colimit, or finiteness hypotheses.

mathlib_searches.query: A localization at a prime of the tensor product is the localization of the tensor product of the local rings at contracted primes
Localizing a tensor base change isomorphism at compatible prime ideals gives a localization of tensor product of local rings and an isomorphism of localized modules
mathlib_searches.results: IsLocalization.tensorProduct_tensorProduct, tensor, tensorRight, algebraTensorEquiv, and moduleTensorEquiv are relevant ingredients; none supplies the coupled statement with canonical transition fraction maps and formulas.

theorem localized_approximation_baseChange
    {S : Type u} [CommRing S]
    {Λ : Type u} [Preorder Λ]
    (A B : Λ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (η : A ⟶ B)
    (κ : B ⟶ (Functor.const Λ).obj (CommRingCat.of S))
    (D : Λ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{v}) [∀ i : Λ, Module (B.obj i) (D.obj i)]
    (hs : ∀ (i j : Λ) (f : i ⟶ j) (b : B.obj i) (x : D.obj i),
      (D.map f).hom (b • x) = (B.map f).hom b • (D.map f).hom x)
    (hring : ∀ (i j : Λ) (f : i ⟶ j),
      letI := (η.app i).hom.toAlgebra
      letI := (A.map f).hom.toAlgebra
      ∃ e : B.obj i ⊗[A.obj i] A.obj j ≃+* B.obj j,
        ∀ (x : B.obj i) (y : A.obj j),
          e (x ⊗ₜ[A.obj i] y) = (B.map f).hom x * (η.app j).hom y)
    (hmodule : ∀ (i j : Λ) (f : i ⟶ j),
      letI := (B.map f).hom.toAlgebra
      ∃ e : B.obj j ⊗[B.obj i] D.obj i ≃ₗ[B.obj j] D.obj j,
        ∀ (y : B.obj j) (x : D.obj i),
          e (y ⊗ₜ[B.obj i] x) = y • (D.map f).hom x)
    (q : PrimeSpectrum S) :
    let Aq := primeRingDiagram A (η ≫ κ) q
    let Bq := primeRingDiagram B κ q
    let Nq := primeModuleDiagram B κ q D hs
    (∀ (i j : Λ) (f : i ⟶ j),
      letI := (primeDiagramHom A B η κ q i).toAlgebra
      letI := (Aq.map f).hom.toAlgebra
      ∃ (t : Bq.obj i ⊗[Aq.obj i] Aq.obj j →+* Bq.obj j)
        (W : Submonoid (Bq.obj i ⊗[Aq.obj i] Aq.obj j)),
        (∀ (b : Bq.obj i) (a : Aq.obj j),
          t (b ⊗ₜ[Aq.obj i] a) =
            (Bq.map f).hom b * primeDiagramHom A B η κ q j a) ∧
        (letI := t.toAlgebra; IsLocalization W (Bq.obj j))) ∧
    (∀ (i j : Λ) (f : i ⟶ j),
      letI := (Bq.map f).hom.toAlgebra
      ∃ e : Bq.obj j ⊗[Bq.obj i] Nq.obj i ≃ₗ[Bq.obj j] Nq.obj j,
        ∀ (b : Bq.obj j) (x : Nq.obj i),
          e (b ⊗ₜ[Bq.obj i] x) = b • (Nq.map f).hom x)
